A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HD-EPIC and contain the complete main paper and supplementary material, including Appendix Table A6. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, VQA experiments, a human baseline, input ablations, action and sound recognition results, and long-term video-object-segmentation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised VQA results and results for an expanded video-object-segmentation test set.

M1.justification: The annotation algorithms, model configurations, and inference procedures are retained. Section 4.3 now explicitly describes correcting all fixture assignments, but iterative review and correction were already documented in v1 Appendix C.3; this does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 41.3-hour, nine-kitchen dataset and retain the four benchmark tasks and 30 VQA prototypes. The larger segmentation sample changes evaluation settings within existing coverage. DAVIS and YouTube-VOS remain descriptive dataset comparisons, rather than newly evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments: the same language/video-language models, recognition methods, human baseline, and Static, Cutie, and SAM2 segmentation baselines remain. Appendix Table A4 also retains the same input conditions.

E3.justification: The segmentation evaluation expands from 400 to 1,000 sequences and from 1–3 to 1–5 objects plus two hands per sequence; annotated frames increase from 6,692 to 20,548 (Section 5.3, Table A5). Appendix D.1.6 also removes the stated stationary-object exclusion based on short stationary duration and fewer than three movements, although this deletion does not establish that VQA experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing input-ablation, input-length, and response-bias analyses receive revised evidence in Table A4 and Figures 12 and A11. The 98% fixture-assignment validation result is removed from Section 4.3. No substantial new family of ablations or robustness tests is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure. Existing descriptive means and standard deviations follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 14 replaces the segmentation results: overall J&F changes from SAM2 59.2 versus Cutie 48.8 to SAM2 47.4 versus Cutie 48.6, reversing their ranking on the revised test set. These are not same-setting performance changes. Table 2 revises Gemini's recipe, ingredient, and overall accuracies from 64.3, 48.6, and 38.5% to 60.5, 46.2, and 37.6%; Table A6 updates individual prototype scores. Table A4 updates category scores but inconsistently retains the old 38.5% average.

T1.justification: The depth-alignment formulation in Section 4.3 and annotation-agreement equations and segment-merging rule in Appendix C.2.2 are unchanged. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a densely annotated, unscripted egocentric dataset with 3D and gaze grounding, a challenging VQA benchmark, and three additional benchmark tasks. The revised headline accuracy does not change the meaning or scope of these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 broadens the interpretation of audio generalization failures to include devices as well as scenes. Appendix D.2 changes which categories benefit most from ground-truth narrations, replacing ingredient with object motion, and corrects its supporting example to 63.6% fine-grained-action accuracy. The sparse-frame segmentation limitation remains.

D1.justification: Section 6 replaces a future-release promise with stated dataset availability through a DOI and annotation access through the project website. Its explicit open-license and benchmark starter-code commitments disappear. Appendix D.4 specifies comparison dataset editions and duration-calculation assumptions of 24 and 6 fps; Section 4.3 clarifies manual correction of fixture assignments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the DAVIS 2017 and YouTube-VOS 2019 challenges to support Appendix D.4's dataset comparison. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged. Several other references receive publication or title updates for the same works.

P1.justification: There are localized paragraph revisions, wording corrections, an expanded author name, and revised acknowledgements and bibliography metadata. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table A1's header is reformatted, Table A6's prototype labels are corrected, and printed page numbers are removed. Updated chart bars accompany revised results in Figures 11, 12, and A11. The figure/table inventory and overall layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Concrete data-access instructions and Appendix D.4's explicit comparison dataset editions and frame-rate assumptions improve usability and transparency. Appendix D.2 also corrects an ablation example. These gains are limited by the newly inconsistent 38.5% average in Table A4, versus 37.6% in Table 2, and removal of explicit license and starter-code commitments. Overall, the evidence supports a modest improvement.
